ai.description: This slender, worm-like snake reaches 20 cm. It is uniform glossy brown or grey with a paler snout and tail tip. Key features include 20 midbody scale rows and a rounded, blunt head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlops porrectus* is best distinguished by its 20 mid-body scale rows, whereas most similar Indian blind snakes possess only 18.
ai.habitat: *Indotyphlops porrectus* inhabits moist soils in tropical forests, agricultural lands, and gardens, ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: Stoliczka’s slender blind snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its life burrowing through loose soil in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlops porrectus* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–10 elongated eggs. Breeding generally occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Indotyphlops porrectus is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 1,500 meters in diverse habitats across most Indian states.
